title: Bake, and the Latency screen
thisBuild: Bake: on a sound's Sample sheet, Play page, tap Bake it. In a few seconds it renders the sound at every semitone an octave up and down, length kept. Played from the bake, Grain sounds cleaner (much less flutter on chords, bass and glassy tones) and costs no more than Stretch.
Within an octave of the sound's own pitch it plays from the bake. Further away, Sustain, and reversed plays stay live grain.
Sounds up to 6 seconds bake. The bakes in one mess share about 96 MB of memory; the Play page says when that is full.

The Audio check is now Latency (Notes for Claude, then Latency). New section, Keep it light: how many live grain voices are playing, which pads needed live grain this session, and Bake them for all of them in one tap.
If the phone stays over 70% busy for 20 seconds with live grain playing, a bar at the top offers to bake those pads, once a session. Bake them, Latency, or Not now.
From build 61: the Sample sheet (the Doctor's new name) with the Play page, Stretch or Grain, Sustain, On the beat, and Cut, Ring or Flow in the repeat rate menu.
watch: Bake a long tonal sound (a chord or a bass note), play it up and down Keys, and compare with Bake off. Baked should sound steadier.
Bake a sound while the music plays: listen for clicks during the few seconds it bakes.
Open Latency after playing keys for a while: the pads you played should be listed under Keep it light.
Run the speaker test and Save as a note, if you have not yet: that number still decides the next audio work.
limits: A bake lasts while the app is open and is redone (a few seconds) when you open the mess again. Bake on stays saved with the sound.
The bake does not follow Bend or Glide exactly: those move the baked pitch like tape, a little shorter or longer, as before.
Synths, loops and the RC-505 library are coming in later builds.
